questions.prompt: How should an API choose an HTTP method?
options: Use GET for payments because caches automatically make it safe.
Assume every PATCH request is idempotent without examining its defined behavior.
Match the method to its defined semantics, including safety and idempotency; do not hide state-changing work in GET.
Choose any method as long as the backend route handler can parse it.
questions.answer_key: Match the method to its defined semantics, including safety and idempotency; do not hide state-changing work in GET.
questions.explanation: Match the method to its defined semantics, including safety and idempotency; do not hide state-changing work in GET. This is especially relevant to “The DELETE Method” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “The DELETE Method”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Repeat representative requests and inspect side effects to verify the selected method semantics.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
questions.answer_key: Repeat representative requests and inspect side effects to verify the selected method semantics.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “The DELETE Method”?
options: Method semantics are misleading or retries may repeat a non-idempotent side effect.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
questions.answer_key: Method semantics are misleading or retries may repeat a non-idempotent side effect.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
